case_name: Padal Venkata Rama Reddy @ Ramu v Kovvuri Satyanarayana Reddy and others
facts: The appellant, who was a defacto complainant and Respondent Nos. 1-3 (accused persons) are the residents of Komaripalem village of East Godavari District.
In the year 2006, the appellant contested Zila Parishad Territorial Constituency Elections as an independent candidate and won it.
A-4 hired A-5 to A-12 for the said purpose and they conspired together and hatched a plan to assault the appellant.
On 07.11.2007 between 7:00 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., A-4, A-7 to A-12 who were in a Scorpio Car came across his car.

After completion of investigation, the S.I. filed charge sheet against A-1 to A-12 on 30.08.2008 for the offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 147, 148, 427, 307, 201 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code (in short
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in quashing the criminal proceedings against the Respondent Nos. 1-3 by invoking jurisdiction u/s. 482 of the Code?
petitioner_arguments: The only point for consideration in this appeal is whether the High Court was justified in quashing the criminal proceedings against the Respondent Nos. 1-3 by invoking jurisdiction u/s. 482 of the Code?
court_reasoning: S. 482 of the Code deals with inherent power of High Court.

In R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab AIR 1960 SC 866=(1960) 3 SCR 388 1960 Indlaw SC 471, this Court laid down the following principles:-(i) Where institution/continuance of criminal proceedings against an accused may amount to the abuse of the process of the court or that the quashing of the impugned proceedings would secure the ends of justice;

In State of Karnataka vs. L.Muniswamy & Ors. AIR 1977 SC 1489 1977 Indlaw SC 184, this Court has held as under:-(i) In the exercise of this wholesome power, the High Court is entitled to quash a proceeding if it comes to the conclusion that allowing the proceeding to continue would be an abuse of the process of the court or that the ends of justice require that the proceeding ought to be quashed.
Though the High Court has inherent power and its scope is very wide, it is a rule of practice that it will only be exercised in exceptional cases.
holding: The appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment dated 28.10.2010 passed by the High Court is set aside. The criminal proceedings pending against Respondent Nos. 1-3 are hereby restored to their original position, i.e., as if the impugned judgment had not been passed.
